summary: The enclosure exterior, solid front panel, rear service openings, internal riser-clamp placement, and overall coherence pass visual review. Mini-ITX, cooler, GPU, PSU, and power-button header-path interfaces remain not verified because the committed views do not show the required reference component envelopes or internal routing evidence.

checks.description: The committed assembly is visually coherent and complete in the reviewed exterior views, with a continuous cap, aligned side and end panels, an integrated base, and no obvious collisions, floating exterior parts, or missing primary enclosure structure.

evidence.description: The isometric view shows the cap, service end, vented side, frame, fasteners, and base assembled into one coherent enclosure without an obvious visible collision or floating exterior component.
The top view shows a continuous, correctly seated rectangular cap with aligned perimeter edges and corner fastening.

checks.description: The rear service geometry is visible, but the images contain no 170 x 170 mm Mini-ITX reference board, mounting-pattern overlay, or exposed retention details sufficient to prove standard-board fit, retention, and rear-I/O alignment.

evidence.description: The assembled enclosure and rear service areas are visible, but the opaque panels conceal the motherboard mounting interface and no reference motherboard is shown.
The orthographic service-end view shows opening regions but does not visually establish the 170 x 170 mm hole pattern, board retention, or exact rear-I/O fit.

checks.description: The required Thermalright AXP120-X67 envelope and a visible clearance gauge are absent, so cooler fit and preserved intake clearance to the side panel cannot be established from the committed views.

evidence.description: The enclosure is closed and the cooler envelope is not displayed; the image therefore cannot show cooler-to-side-panel intake clearance.

checks.description: Rear GPU service geometry is visible, but no approved compact GPU envelope, installed I/O bracket, PCIe riser body/path, or power-cable bend envelope is shown, so the complete GPU-fit interface is not visually established.

evidence.description: The image shows the assembled service end and enclosure proportions but no installed or reference GPU, riser cable, or power-cable bend volume.
The service-end view indicates distinct rear regions, but it does not prove bracket engagement, GPU envelope clearance, riser routing, or cable bend space.

checks.description: A separate rear PSU service region is present, but the views do not show a 160 x 80 x 40 mm reference PSU seated in its cradle or visually prove AC inlet engagement, airflow, retention, and cable-routing clearance.

evidence.description: The closed assembly exposes service-end geometry but not an installed PSU envelope, its retention interfaces, airflow path, or internal cable routing.

checks.description: The single power-button cap is visibly accessible from outside, but no internal wire channel or route to the motherboard header is visible; therefore the full external-control interface is not verified.

evidence.description: The solid end panel visibly presents one external circular button cap near its upper edge, while the closed enclosure leaves the required internal header path unseen.

checks.description: The reviewed front panel is a continuous solid removable panel with no vent slots or perforation field; it visibly retains one power-button position and six panel-fastening screws.

evidence.description: The orthographic view directly shows an uninterrupted solid rectangular panel, one larger circular power-button feature near the top, and six smaller fastening positions arranged in three pairs.
The isometric view confirms the panel is a separate seated exterior piece and shows no front ventilation slots or round-hole array.

checks.description: The rear service face remains open and visibly divided into distinct motherboard-I/O, GPU, and compact-PSU access regions rather than being replaced by the solid front-panel treatment.

evidence.description: The isometric service-end view visibly shows multiple separate aperture regions, including a tall left region and separate upper and lower right-hand service regions.
The orthographic view confirms that the service face retains three spatially distinct access zones within its fastened perimeter.

checks.description: The focused exterior views show the riser clamp bars and their four screws contained behind the enclosure surfaces; they do not visibly penetrate the solid front panel, either side panel, or the top cap.

evidence.description: The service-end, vented side, and continuous top cap are visibly uninterrupted by riser-clamp bars or clamp screws.
The orthographic side view shows the clamp structure remaining behind the perforated side-panel plane, with no visible component protruding through that panel.
The opposite isometric view shows the solid front and adjacent side remaining externally clear of the internal clamp hardware.

checks.description: The solid front, separate rear service face, round-hole side panel, continuous top cap, and base form a visually complete enclosure with aligned seams and no obvious exterior interpenetration, floating component, or missing primary panel.

evidence.description: The isometric view shows the rear service face, perforated side, continuous cap, frame, and base meeting coherently along aligned edges.
The opposite isometric view shows the solid front panel, second perforated side, and footed base assembled without an obvious exterior collision or missing panel.
The solid-panel orthographic view confirms a complete front closure with a regular six-fastener perimeter and one button feature.
